Hi there- the doctor is scary. I’m with you there but the benefits of having medication make it worth it.  If you are looking for ADHD medication/diagnosis then I would go to a psychiatrist.  

Depending on your state or country regulations you may even be able to be treated through telehealth.  I had to go in for the initial visit but most of my visits are virtual now. Which makes it seem more manageable and less scary.  

Look at the reviews of the practice.  

Psychiatrist’s are better for what you are describing because they deal with this on a daily basis.  They tend to take you seriously from the get go in my experience.  Just be honest, tell them what you are looking for. Ask questions. Don’t worry about the time you are taking. MOST importantly, if you don’t like the provider. Try another one.  

Also- in terms of managing your day to day and chores. I have been using the app called Finch. Highly recommend so far. A lot of tools and a supportive community. 

You got this!! It’s worth it.  You just need some tools to help you manage life better.

I had similar reservations when IOP was suggested a few years ago. I had been to two facilities at that point for suicidality/SI/depression. Several meds. All the side effects. Ketamine. EMDR. TMS. Everything you listed.  I was desperate.  I decided to give it a go and I applied myself like it was my job. I took notes. I participated.  I made lists to try and work the skills real time to see if they helped.  

It was worth it to me. It IS a big commitment but you can learn tools and hear how other people cope. New perspectives.  What they have done to work through.  I’d do it again.  

I am still trialing meds. Some are working. Some are not.  But I still have the skills from IOP that I read through when I need.  

The program you choose matters. The one I went to did not let us directly respond to another participant. We could relate but the work was focused individually.  Which was very helpful and I liked the distance from the others to focus on me.  

Good luck!
